questions.question: Angle between the internal bisectors of two angles ∠B and ∠C of a ΔABC is 132°, then the value of ∠A is
questions.questionHtml: Angle between the internal bisectors of two angles ∠B and ∠C of a ΔABC is 132°, then the value of ∠A is
questions.solution:
Given:-

Angle between bisectors of ∠B and ∠C = 132°   

Concept:

If bisector of angles ∠B and ∠C of a triangle ABC meets at I then ∠BIC = 90° + 1/2 ∠A

Calculation:

∠BIC = 132° 

∠BIC = 90° + 1/2 ∠A

∠A/2 = (132° – 90°)

⇒∠A/2 = 42° 

⇒ ∠A = 42 × 2 

⇒ ∠A = 84° 

∴ The value of ∠A is 84°

questions.question: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, the areas of ΔABC and ΔPQR are 64 cm 2 and 81 cm 2 , respectively and AD and PT are the medians of ΔABC and ΔPQR, respectively. If PT = 10.8 cm, then AD = ?
questions.questionHtml: ΔABC ~ ΔPQR, the areas of ΔABC and ΔPQR are 64 cm<sup>2</sup> and 81 cm<sup>2</sup>, respectively and AD and PT are the medians of ΔABC and ΔPQR, respectively. If PT = 10.8 cm, then AD = ?
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔABC ~ ΔPQR

Area of ΔABC = 64 cm2

Area of ΔPQR = 81 cm2

PT = 10.8 cm 

AD is the median of ΔABC.

PT is the median of ΔPQR

Concept: 

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of the squares of the corresponding sides & medians. 

\(\text{Area of (ΔABC)}\over{\text{Area of (ΔPQR)}}\) = \(({AD\over PT})^2\)

Calculation:

\(\text{Area of (ΔABC)}\over{\text{Area of (ΔPQR)}}\) = \(({AD\over PT})^2\)

⇒ \(64\over81\) = \(({AD\over PT})^2\) 

⇒​ \(AD\over PT\) = \(\sqrt{64\over81}\) = \(8\over9\)

⇒​ \(AD\over 10.8\) = \(8\over9\)

⇒​ AD = \({8\times10.8}\over9\) = 9.6 cm

∴ AD = 9.6 cm

questions.question: If AB = QR, BC = PR and CA = PQ, then
questions.questionHtml: If AB = QR, BC = PR and CA = PQ, then
questions.solution:
Given:

AB = QR, BC = PR and CA = PQ

Formula used:

Side-side-side congruence rule:- If all the three sides of a triangle are equal to the corresponding sides of another triangle, then the two triangles are congruent to each other.

Calculation:

Let ABC and PQR be two triangles.

The congruence of the two triangles is written with respect to the corresponding sides and since  AB = QR, BC = PR and CA = PQ, ΔCBA ≅ ΔPRQ.

∴ If AB = QR, BC = PR and CA = PQ, then ΔCBA ≅ ΔPRQ.

questions.question: If one of the angles of a triangles is 74°, then the angle between the bisectors of the other two interior angles is:
questions.questionHtml: If one of the angles of a triangles is 74°, then the angle between the bisectors of the other two interior angles is:
questions.solution:
Given:

One angle = 74°

Calculation:

In the above figure, AD and BE are angle bisectors of ∠A and ∠B respectively.

⇒ ∠A = ∠a/2 + ∠a/2

⇒ ∠B = ∠b/2 + ∠b/2

In ΔABC,

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 2∠a/2 + 2∠b/2 + 74 = 180°

⇒ ∠a/2 + ∠b/2 = 53°

Then,

In ΔAPB,

⇒ ∠PAB + ∠ABP + ∠BPA = 180°

⇒ ∠BPA = 180° - (a/2 + b/2) 

⇒ ∠BPA = 180° - 53° = 127°

∴ The angle between the bisectors of the other two interior angles is 127°.

Alternate Method In ΔABC, such that ∠ACB = 74° and bisectors ∠A and ∠B meet at D and E.

Now, In ΔABC,

∠ACB + ∠ABC + ∠BAC = 180° 

⇒ 74° + ∠ABC + ∠BAC = 180° 

⇒ ∠ABC + ∠BAC = 180° - 74° = 106° 

⇒ \(1\over2\)(∠ABC + ∠BAC) = 53° 

∠PBA + ∠BAP = 53° (PA and PB bisect ∠BAC and ∠ABC)

Now, In ΔPAB,

∠PBA + ∠BAP + ∠BPA = 180° 

⇒ 53° + ∠BPA = 180° 

⇒ ∠BPA = 180° - 53° = 127° 

∴ ∠BPA = 127°

questions.question: The difference between the largest and the smallest angles of a triangle whose angles are in the ratio of 4 : 3 : 8, is:
questions.questionHtml: The difference between the largest and the smallest angles of a triangle whose angles are in the ratio of 4 : 3 : 8, is:
questions.solution:
Given:

As shown in above figure

Let us consider a triangle ABC were ∠A = 4x°, ∠B = 3x°, ∠C = 8x°

As The Largest angle is ∠C है, and the Smallest angle is ∠B

Calculation:

As we know the sum of all angle of triangle = 180°

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 4x° + 3x° + 8x° = 180°

⇒ 15x° = 180°

⇒ x° = 180°/15° = 12°

⇒ ∠A = 4 × 12° = 48°, ∠B = 3 × 12° = 36°, ∠C = 8 × 12° = 96°

∴ ∠C - ∠ B = 96° - 36° = 60°

questions.question: Let ΔABC ~ ΔPQR and \( \frac{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{ABC})}{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{QPR})}=\frac{64}{169} \text { }\) If AB = 10 cm, BC = 7 cm and AC = 16 cm, then PR (in cm) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: Let ΔABC ~ ΔPQR and \( \frac{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{ABC})}{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{QPR})}=\frac{64}{169} \text { }\) If AB = 10 cm, BC = 7 cm and AC = 16 cm, then PR (in cm) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔABC ~ ΔPQR

ar(ΔABC)/ar(ΔQPR) = 64/169

AB = 10 cm, BC = 7 cm and AC = 16 cm

Concept used:

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of the squares of the corresponding sides

Calculation:

ar(ΔABC)/ar(ΔQPR) = AC2/PR2

⇒ 64/169 = 162/PR2

⇒ 8/13 = 16/PR

⇒ PR = (13 × 16)/8 = 26 cm

∴ PR (in cm) is equal to 26 cm

Mistake PointsΔABC ~ ΔPQR is important 

It does not matter what is given in the ratio form, 

That is \( \frac{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{ABC})}{\operatorname{ar}(\triangle \mathrm{QPR})}\)

Hence we always solve the question according to ΔABC ~ ΔPQR.

questions.question: In ∆ DEW, AB∥EW. If AD = 4 cm, DE = 12 cm and DW = 24 cm, then find the length of DB.
questions.questionHtml: In ∆ DEW, AB∥EW. If AD = 4 cm, DE = 12 cm and DW = 24 cm, then find the length of DB.
questions.solution:
Given:

In ∆DEW, AB∥EW.

AD = 4 cm, DE = 12 cm, DW = 24 cm.

Formula Used:

Using the Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT):

If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides, then it divides those sides in the same ratio.

Calculation:

Using BPT, we have:

\(\frac{AD}{DE} = \frac{DB}{DW}\)

Substitute the given values:

\(\frac{4}{12} = \frac{DB}{24}\)

Simplify the ratio on the left side:

\(\frac{1}{3} = \frac{DB}{24}\)

Cross-multiply to solve for DB:

⇒ DB × 3 = 24

⇒ DB = 24 / 3

⇒ DB = 8 cm

The length of DB is 8 cm.

questions.question: Δ ABC ∼ Δ DEF. If the areas of Δ ABC and Δ DEF are 100 cm 2 and 81 cm 2 respectively and the altitude of Δ DEF is 6.3 cm, then the corresponding altitude of Δ ABC is:

Given:

Area of ΔABC = 100 cm2

Area of ΔDEF = 81 cm2

Altitude of Δ DEF = 6.3 cm

Concept used:

If two triangle is similar then,

(Area of ABC)/(Area of DEF) = (Altitude of ABC)2/(Altitude of DEF)2

Calculation:

Let, the altitude of ΔABC be x

So,

100/81 = (x)2/(6.3)2

⇒ √100/√81 = x/6.3

⇒ 10/9 = x/6.3

⇒ 9 × x = 10 × 6.3 

⇒ x = 7 cm

∴ The altitude of Δ ABC is is 7 cm.

Given:

questions.solution:
Given:

In ΔABC, AB = 7 cm, BC = 10 cm, and AC = 8 cm

Concept used:

An angle bisector of an angle of a triangle divides the opposite side into two segments that are proportional to the other two sides of the triangle.

Calculation:

AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC

So, AB/AC = BD/DC

⇒ 7/8 = BD/DC

⇒ 8BD = 7DC

⇒ BD = 7DC/8   .....(1)

Here, BD + DC = BC

⇒ 7DC/8 + DC = BC = 10  [∵ BD = 7DC/8]

⇒ 15DC/8 = 10

⇒ DC = 10 × (8/15) = 80/15 = 16/3

∴ The value of DC (in cm) is 16/3

questions.question: If ΔABC and ΔPQR are similar. AB = 8 cm, PQ = 12 cm, QR = 18 cm and RP = 24 cm, then the perimeter of ΔABC is _________ cm.
questions.questionHtml: <!-- x-tinymce/html -->If ΔABC and ΔPQR are similar. AB = 8 cm, PQ = 12 cm, QR = 18 cm and RP = 24 cm, then the perimeter of ΔABC is _________ cm.
questions.solution:
ΔABC ∼ ΔPQR, AB = 8 cm, PQ = 12 cm, QR = 18 cm, RP = 24 cm.

AB/PQ = BC/QR = AC/PR, ⇒ 8/12 = BC/18 = AC/24

⇒ BC = (18 × 8) / 12 = 12 cm

⇒ AC = (12 × 24) / 18 = 16 cm

Perimeter of ΔABC = AB + BC + AC = 8 + 12 + 16 = 36 cm

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, CA is produced to P, ∠ BAP = 126°. If ∠ABC ∶ ∠ACB = 5 ∶ 2, the degree measures of ∠B and ∠C are respectively:
questions.questionHtml: In a triangle ABC, CA is produced to P, ∠ BAP = 126°. If ∠ABC ∶ ∠ACB = 5 ∶ 2, the degree measures of ∠B and ∠C are respectively:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

According to the Exterior Angle Theorem, the exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

Sum of interior opposite angles ∠B + ∠C = Exterior ∠BAP = 126°.

Ratio of ∠B : ∠C = 5 : 2.

Total units = 5 + 2 = 7 units ⇒ 126°.

1 unit = 126° ÷ 7 = 18°.

∠B = 5 × 18° = 90° and ∠C = 2 × 18° = 36°.

∴ The correct answer is 90° and 36°.

Alternate Method

Given: Exterior ∠BAP = 126° and ∠ABC : ∠ACB = 5 : 2.

Formula Used: Exterior angle = Sum of interior opposite angles.

Let ∠ABC = 5x and ∠ACB = 2x.

By the Exterior Angle Theorem in triangle ABC:

⇒ ∠ABC + ∠ACB = Exterior ∠BAP

⇒ 5x + 2x = 126°

⇒ 7x = 126°

⇒ x = 126° ÷ 7

⇒ x = 18°

Now, calculate the measure of each angle:

⇒ ∠B = 5x = 5 × 18° = 90°

⇒ ∠C = 2x = 2 × 18° = 36°

∴ The correct answer is 90° and 36°.

Additional Information

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote (opposite) interior angles.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of a triangle is always 180°. In this case, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 54° + 90° + 36° = 180°.

Linear Pair of Angles

Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. Here, interior ∠BAC + exterior ∠BAP = 180° ⇒ 54° + 126° = 180°.

questions.question: The lengths of the two sides forming the right angle of a right-angled triangle are 21 cm and 20 cm. What is the radius of the circle circumscribing the triangle?
questions.questionHtml: The lengths of the two sides forming the right angle of a right-angled triangle are 21 cm and 20 cm. What is the radius of the circle circumscribing the triangle?
questions.solution:
Given:

The lengths of the two sides forming the right angle of a right-angled triangle are 21 cm and 20 cm

Formula:

Hypotenuse2 = Base2 + Perpendicular2

Circum-radius of the right-angled triangle = Hypotenuse/2

Calculation:

Base = 21 cm and Perpendicular = 20 cm

⇒ (Hypotenuse)2 = 212 + 202

⇒ 441 + 400

⇒ 841

⇒ (Hypotenuse) = √841 = 29

∴ Circum-radius of the right-angled triangle = 29/2 = 14.5 cm

questions.questionHtml: ΔPQR is similar to ΔUVW. Perimeter ΔPQR and ΔUVW are 120 cm and 240 cm respectively. If PQ = 30 cm, then what is the length of UV?
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔPQR is similar to ΔUVW

Perimeter ΔPQR and ΔUVW are 120 cm and 240 cm respectively

PQ = 30 cm

Concept Used:

In the similarity of triangles ratios of respective sides of triangles are the equal perimeter of the triangles.

Calculation:

Using the concept

⇒ (perimeter of ΔPQR)/(perimeter of ΔUVW) = PQ/UV

⇒ 120/240 = 30/UV

⇒ 1/2 = 30/UV

UV = 60

∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The measure of one of the exterior angles of a triangle is twice one of the interior opposite angles and the measure of the other interior opposite angles is 60º. The triangle is a/an:
questions.questionHtml: The measure of one of the exterior angles of a triangle is twice one of the interior opposite angles and the measure of the other interior opposite angles is 60º. The triangle is a/an:
questions.solution:
Given:

The measure of one of the exterior angles = 2 × one of the interior opposite angles

The measure of other interior opposite angles = 60° 

Concept used:

Equilateral triangle: the measure of each interior angle is 60°  

Right-angle triangle: the measure of one of the interior angle should be 90° 

Scalene triangle: the measure of each angle is different.

Isosceles triangle: the measure of one of the two interior angles are equal.

The measure of one of the exterior angle = the sum of its opposite interior angles.

The sum of all interior angles in a triangle = 180° 

Calculation:

Let one of the interior opposites angles be x

The measure of one of the exterior angle = x + 60° 

⇒ 2 × one of the interior opposite angles = x + 60° 

⇒ 2x = x + 60° 

⇒ 2x - x = 60° 

⇒ x = 60° 

Now the third interior angle = 180° - x - 60° 

⇒ 180° - 60° - 60° 

⇒ 180° - 120° 

⇒ 60° 

Then we can see that each interior angle = 60° and this is possible when triangle will be an equilateral triangle.

∴ The triangle is an Equilateral triangle.

questions.question: If ABC is a triangle in which DE ‖ BC and AD ∶ DB = 9 ∶ 8, then DE ∶ BC is _________.
questions.questionHtml: If ABC is a triangle in which DE ‖ BC and AD ∶ DB = 9 ∶ 8, then DE ∶ BC is _________.
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

In triangle ABC, DE// BC

AD/.DB = 9/8 

CONCEPT USED:

Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT) = If line DE is parallel to side BC of triangle ABC that intersects the other sides into two points, line DE divides AB and AC in proportion.

AD/AB = AE/AC = DE/BC

CALCULATION:

In triangle ABC, AD/DB = 9/8

⇒ AD/AB = DE/BC 

⇒ 9/(9+8) = DE/BC 

⇒ 9/17 = DE/BC

Hence, DE :BC = 9:17.

questions.question: In the triangle given below, D and E are mid points of AF and AG respectively, F and G are mid points of AB and AC respectively. If DE = 2.4 cm, then BC is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: In the triangle given below, D and E are mid points of AF and AG respectively, F and G are mid points of AB and AC respectively. If DE = 2.4 cm, then BC is equal to∶
questions.solution:
In the triangle given below, D and E are mid points of AF and AG respectively, F and G are mid points of AB and AC respectively & DE = 2.4 cm

As we know,

DE/FG = AD/AF

⇒ DE/FG = 1/2

⇒ 2.4/FG = 1/2

FG = 2 × 2.4 = 4.8 cm

Similarly

FG/BC = AF/AB

⇒ FG/BC = 1/2

⇒ 4.8/BC = 1/2

⇒ BC = 4.8 × 2 = 9.6 cm

questions.question: In the figure, in ΔPQR, PT ⊥ QR at T and PS is the bisector of ∠QPR. If ∠PQR = 78°, and ∠TPS = 24°, then the measure of ∠PRQ is:
questions.questionHtml: In the figure, in ΔPQR, PT ⊥ QR at T and PS is the bisector of ∠QPR. If ∠PQR = 78°, and ∠TPS = 24°, then the measure of ∠PRQ is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick As we know,

∠TPS = (∠TQP - ∠PRQ)/2

24 = (78 - ∠PRQ)/2

78 - ∠PRQ = 24 × 2 = 48

∠PRQ = 78 - 48 = 30

Alternate MethodGiven: 

 In ΔPQR, PT ⊥ QR at T and PS is the bisector of ∠QPR

∠PQR = 78° and ∠TPS = 24° 

Calculation:

In ΔPQT,

∠QPT = 180° - ∠PQR - ∠PTQ = 180° - 78° - 90° = 12°

∠SPQ = ∠QPT + ∠TPS = 12° + 24° = 36°

Since PS is the bisector of ∠QPR.

∠QPR = 2 × ∠SPQ = 2 × 36° = 72°

In ΔPQR,

∠PRQ = 180° - ∠PQR - ∠QPR = 180° - 78° - 72° = 30°

Hence the required answer is 30°

questions.question: The side ST of ΔRST is produced to P. If ∠RTP = 115° and ∠S = \(\frac{2}{3}\) ∠R, then the measure of ∠R is:
questions.questionHtml: The side ST of ΔRST is produced to P. If ∠RTP = 115° and ∠S = \(\frac{2}{3}\)∠R, then the measure of ∠R is:
questions.solution:
Ans:3

Given:

The side ST of ΔRST is produced to P.

∠RTP = 115°, ∠S = \(\frac{2}{3}\)∠R

Formula used:

The sum of two interior angles = the opposite exterior angle

Calculation:

The sum of two interior angles is equal to the opposite exterior angle.

⇒ ∠S + ∠R = 115°

⇒ \(\frac{2}{3}\)∠R + ∠R = 115°

⇒ \(\frac{5}{3}\)∠R = 115°

⇒ ∠R = 69° 

∴ value of ∠R is 69°

questions.question: Let △ABC ~ △QPR and \(\frac{{{\rm{ar}}\left( {{\rm{\Delta ABC}}} \right)}}{{{\rm{ar}}\left( {{\rm{\Delta PQR}}} \right)}}\, = \,\frac{{49}}{{144}}\) . If AB = 12 cm, BC = 9 cm and AC = 7 cm, then QR (in cm) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: Let △ABC ~ △QPR and \(\frac{{{\rm{ar}}\left( {{\rm{\Delta ABC}}} \right)}}{{{\rm{ar}}\left( {{\rm{\Delta PQR}}} \right)}}\, = \,\frac{{49}}{{144}}\). If AB = 12 cm, BC = 9 cm and AC = 7 cm, then QR (in cm) is equal to:
questions.solution:
\(AC^2\over QR^2\) = \(ar ABC\over ar PQR\) 

Taking the square root of both the sides ⇒ \(7 \over QR\) = \(7\over 12\) ⇒ QR = 12 cm

questions.question: The side QR of a triangle PQR is extended to a point S. If ∠PRS = 104° and ∠RQP = \(\frac{3}{5}\) ∠QPR, then the value of ∠QPR is:
questions.questionHtml: The side QR of a triangle PQR is extended to a point S. If ∠PRS = 104° and ∠RQP = \(\frac{3}{5}\) ∠QPR, then the value of ∠QPR is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Side QR of a triangle PQR is extended to a point S.

∠PRS = 104° and ∠RQP = \(\frac{3}{5}\) ∠QPR

Concept used:

Exterior angle property of triangle ∠QPR + ∠PQR = ∠PRS

Calculation:

Let ∠QPR = p

then by Exterior angle property of triangle, 

⇒ ∠QPR + ∠PQR = ∠PRS

⇒ p + 3/5 × p = 104°  

⇒ 8/5 × p = 104° 

⇒ p = 104° × 5/8 = 65° 

∴ ∠QPR = 65°

questions.question: In a Δ ABC, DE is parallel to BC, AD = 3 cm, AE = 4 cm and AC = 10 cm, then the value of BD in centimetres is:
questions.questionHtml: In a Δ ABC, DE is parallel to BC, AD = 3 cm, AE = 4 cm and AC = 10 cm, then the value of BD in centimetres is:
questions.solution:
Given:

 In Δ ABC

DE is parallel to BC 

AE = 4 cm

AD = 3 cm

AC = 10 cm 

Concept Used:

AAA' similarity rule

If three angles of two triangles are equal then corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional

Calculation:

If DE is parallel to BC 

∠A = ∠A (Common)

∠ADE = ∠ABC (corresponding angles of parallel sides are equal)

∠AED = ∠ACB (corresponding angles of parallel sides are equal)

By AAA similarity Δ ABC and Δ ADE are similar

then corresponding sides of two triangle  are in ratio

AD/AB = AE/AC = DE/BC 

(AD/AB) = (AE/AC)

⇒ 3/AB = 4/10

⇒ AB = 15/2 = 7.5 cm

As, AB = AD + BD

⇒ 7.5 = 3 + BD

⇒ 7.5 - 3 = BD

⇒ BD = 4.5 cm

∴ The value of BD is 4.5 cm

∴ RO = 16 cm

questions.question: The sides PQ and PR of ΔPQR are produced to points S and T, respectively. The bisectors of ∠SQR and ∠TRQ meet at point U. If ∠QUR = 69°, then the measure of ∠P is:
questions.questionHtml: The sides PQ and PR of ΔPQR are produced to points S and T, respectively. The bisectors of ∠SQR and ∠TRQ meet at point U. If ∠QUR = 69°, then the measure of ∠P is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given, ∠QUR = 69°

If the bisectors of ∠SQR and ∠TRQ meet at point U

∠QUR = 90° - ∠P/2

⇒ ∠QUR = (180° - ∠P)/2

⇒ 69° = (180° - ∠P)/2

⇒ 180° - ∠P = 2 × 69° = 138°

⇒ ∠P = 180° - 138° = 42°

∴ The measure of ∠P is 42°

Alternate Method

Given:

∠QUR = 69°

Concept used:

The sum of all angles on a straight line is 180°

The sum of all angles of a triangle is 180°

Calculation:

∠PQR + ∠RQS = 180°

⇒ ∠RQS = 180° - ∠PQR

⇒ ∠RQS/2 = (180° - ∠PQR)/2

⇒ ∠RQS/2 = 90° - ∠PQR/2

⇒ ∠RQU = 90° - ∠PQR/2  [∵ QU is the bisector of ∠RQS]

Similarly, ∠QRU = 90° - ∠PRQ/2

In ΔQUR, ∠RQU + ∠QRU + ∠QUR = 180°

⇒ [90° - ∠PQR/2] + [90° - ∠PRQ/2] + 69° = 180°

⇒ 180° - [∠PQR/2 + ∠PRQ/2] + 69° = 180°

⇒ 180° - [(∠PQR + ∠PRQ)/2] + 69° = 180°

⇒ 180° - [(180° - ∠P)/2] + 69° = 180°

⇒ [(180° - ∠P)/2] = 69°

⇒ 180° - ∠P = 2 × 69° = 138°

⇒ ∠P = 180° - 138° = 42°

∴ The measure of ∠P is 42°

questions.question: In ΔABC and ΔDEF, we have \(\frac{AB}{DF} = \frac{BC}{DE} = \frac{AC}{EF}\) , then which of the following is true ?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC and ΔDEF, we have \(\frac{AB}{DF} = \frac{BC}{DE} = \frac{AC}{EF}\) , then which of the following is true ?
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔABC and ΔDEF 

\(\frac{AB}{DF} = \frac{BC}{DE} = \frac{AC}{EF}\)

Concept used:

The basic proportionality theorem states if two triangles ABC and DEF are said to be similar if all the corresponding sides of the two triangles are in the same proportion, then,

AB/DE = BC/EF = AC/DF

Calculation:

Now, we have,

AB/DF = BC/DE = AC/EF

⇒ BC/DE = CA/EF = BA/DF

So, Side BC is corresponding to DE, CA is corresponding to EF and BA is corresponding to DF.

Now, ΔBCA is similar to ΔDEF.

∴ ΔBCA ~ ΔDEF.

questions.question: ∆ABC, D is a point on BC such that AD is the bisector of ∠A, AB = 11.7 cm, AC = 7.8 cm and BC = 13 cm. what is the length (in cm) of DC?
questions.questionHtml: ∆ABC, D is a point on BC such that AD is the bisector of ∠A, AB = 11.7 cm, AC = 7.8 cm and BC = 13 cm. what is the length (in cm) of DC?

AB = 11.7, AC = 7.8 and BC = 13 and BC = BD + DC

In ΔABC, AD is bisector of ∠A, then

AB/AC = BD/DC

11.7/7.8 = BD/DC

Ratio of BD : DC = 117 : 78 = 3 : 2

⇒ 3 + 2 = 5 unit

⇒ 1 unit = 13/5

⇒ 2 unit = 13/5 × 2 = 5.2

questions.question: In any triangle, if the angles are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3, then what will be the ratio of the side opposite to them?
questions.questionHtml: In any triangle, if the angles are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3, then what will be the ratio of the side opposite to them?
questions.solution:
Given:

The ratio of angles = 1 : 2 : 3

Concept used:

Sine rule = a/sinA = b/sinB = c/sinC

Calculation:

  

Let A = x, B = 2x and C = 3x

⇒ ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180° [angle sum property]

⇒ x + 2x + 3x = 180° 

⇒ 6x = 180° 

⇒ x = 30° 

⇒ ∠A = 30°, ∠B = 60° and ∠C = 90° 

Now,

As we know that,

⇒ a/sin30° = b/sin60° = c/sin90° 

⇒ a/1/2 = b/√3/2 = c/1

⇒ a = 1, b = √3 and c = 2

So, a : b : c = 1 : √3 : 2

∴ The required ratio is 1 : √3 : 2

questions.question: In Δ ABC, points D and E are on AB and AC, respectively, such that DE is parallel to BC. If AD = 3 cm, BD = 6 cm and AE = 2 cm, then find the length of CE.
questions.questionHtml: In Δ ABC, points D and E are on AB and AC, respectively, such that DE is parallel to BC. If AD = 3 cm, BD = 6 cm and AE = 2 cm, then find the length of CE.
questions.solution:
Given:

DE is parallel to BC

AD = 3 cm, BD = 6 cm and AE = 2 cm

Concept:

If ΔABC and ΔDEF are similar, then AB/DE = BC/EF = CA/FD

Calculation:

In the above figure, ΔABC and ΔADE are similar as -

1. ∠A is common

2. ∠ADE = ∠ABC(∵ DE ∥ BC)

So, AD/AB = AE/AC

⇒ 3/(3 + 6) = 2/(2 + CE)

⇒ 1/3 = 2/(2 + CE)

⇒ CE + 2 = 6

⇒ CE = 4 cm

∴ The length of CE is 4 cm.
